statements.text: Andy Clark and Josefa Toribio hold that even if the contents of visual experience reflect ways of acting, the question of why such activity is felt at all is untouched. A ping-pong playing robot that learns its own sensorimotor contingencies meets the stated conditions without plausibly having experience, and the view seems to imply that every difference in contingencies is a difference in experience.

sources.quote: Even if the contents of our conscious visual experiences reflect ways of acting in the world, the hard problem surely remains.
it seems implausible to depict such a robot
every difference in sensorimotor contingencies corresponds to a difference in conscious visual experience
